Pinning it needs another Dockerfile change and therefore another tag, so it was kept out of the validation path rather than bundled. PRIOR PIN (2026-08-15): both envs on `2026.7.2-isol8.4-c935eff`. Compared with ab1ecd9, the image context changes only bundled skill files. The Paperclip skill adds agent-facing company search/extract, decision creation/get, own-origin `ruleKey` stats, queue/triage helpers, and documents unified attention as board-only. The Isol8 skill adds the accurate hire-time automation handoff: schedules arrive paused and webhook automations require buyer wiring. There is no Dockerfile, plugin, base-image, boot-chain, config-schema, or persistence-code change. It moves no existing owner; each per-owner image roll remains explicit. Image build run `31872851843` succeeded. `upstream` is the base image the extended Dockerfile FROMs — the Isol8 fork (Isol8AI/agent) built from upstream OpenClaw 2026.7.2 (branch off tag v2026.7.2-beta.3 — 7.2 is BETA-ONLY upstream, no stable cut yet) plus the FIVE carried fork patches. Three are re-expressed onto 7.2's rewritten MCP manager (upstream #106359): bundled-MCP shared-runtime-scope (keys the static runtime on (workspaceDir, agentDir, configFingerprint) so sessions reuse one connected runtime — collapses the per-session EFS connect storm), non-blocking tool materialization (peek-then-warm; a cold catalog streams the run on built-ins and warms MCP in the background), and provider-agnostic size-based context pruning (Isol8AI/agent#1). The FOURTH, new in isol8.2, is the native workspace-seed boot hook: `ensureAgentWorkspace` converts an Isol8 sentinel `.openclaw/isol8-setup-seed.json` into native SQLite workspace-setup-state via OpenClaw's own `mergeWorkspaceSetupState`, then deletes the sentinel — so no legacy `workspace-state.json` is ever written and the #1429 "requires migration" brick class is structurally impossible. It is INERT when no sentinel exists (zero behavior change for existing containers), non-throwing (a failure logs and falls through to normal boot), and kill-switched by env `ISOL8_NATIVE_SETUP_SEED=0`. The FIFTH, new in isol8.4 (skips isol8.3, an abandoned OPENCLAW_SQLITE_DIR relocation approach superseded by the nested-mount O6 layout), is the session-store read-failure fix (fork PR #3): `loadGatewaySessionLookupStore` no longer swallows a `session_entries` read error into an empty map — under the 7.2 SQLite lock-contention class a transient throw otherwise resolved every session lookup to "no such session", so `chat.history` returned ok:true with zero messages (byte-identical to a new session — the intermittent "agent forgot everything / start-a-new-conversation over a real transcript" bug) and `chat.send` re-keyed the session, orphaning its transcript. It now throws a typed SessionLookupUnavailableError that chat.history/chat.startup convert to the retryable UNAVAILABLE shape the client history-retry ladder already recovers from; a missing DB stays a non-error (created on first open). The 7.1 compaction aws-sdk-auth cherry-pick (openclaw#103638) was DROPPED — native in beta.3. REQUIRED to build the extended image FROM this fork tag, NOT vanilla ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw: config.py emits mcp.runtimeScope="shared" which only the shared-runtime-scope patch adds to the strict config schema (McpConfigSchema, relocated to zod-schema.root-support.ts in #106359, still `z.strictObject`) — a vanilla 7.2 base crash-loops every MCP owner and (via 7.x's fail-closed startup-migration checkpoint) fails the whole fleet closed. Tag scheme `<upstream-version>-isol8.<n>`. This is a PRIVATE GHCR package, only pulled by the authenticated build-openclaw-image.yml workflow. DEPLOY POSTURE: 7.2 is beta upstream; prod has been on beta by explicit owner acceptance since 2026-07-20. PRIOR PIN (2026-08-14): both envs on `2026.7.2-isol8.4-ab1ecd9` (#1789), which supersedes c700ddd and carries one behavioural change on top of it: openclaw-quarantine.sqlite is no longer listed for litestream replication. That database is hardcoded to `journal_mode = DELETE` upstream (it records corrupted databases, so it must not depend on WAL's -shm sidecar) and litestream replicates by shipping WAL frames, so it was never replicable: across the whole prod fleet its replica prefix held ZERO objects while the state DB beside it held thousands. The cost of listing it was four compaction monitors (levels 1/2/3/9) permanently blocked on a database that never initialises, each burning a 30s timeout, on every container, forever. Removing it returns that CPU and changes nothing else. NOT in this tag, and deliberately so: an intermediate build (e5297a2) also capped doctor --fix at 120s; that was reverted in #1789 before anything ran it, because doctor takes 52-84s across the fleet and a growing tenant would have been killed mid-repair. Do not pin e5297a2. CONTEXT: this pin does not fix the `database is locked` boot failure on over-limit tenants. That is CPU starvation -- during plugins.load the gateway receives ~0.12 of a core while the task sits pinned at 100%, so its SQLite work cannot finish inside the 5s busy timeout. Measured across 11 consecutive failures. The fix for that is vCPU, not this image. The split dev-first pin lasted minutes and was closed by explicit owner decision, restoring the usual pin-both-together practice. NOTE what the pin does and does not do: it sets the image for NEW provisions and is the default the admin image picker offers. It moves NO existing owner — per-user task defs are registered by the backend and pinned per owner on the containers row, so a running or stopped owner stays on its own revision until an explicit queue_image_update -> apply_update. c700ddd had booted nowhere when this was pinned; validation is per-owner at roll time, not at pin time. c700ddd (merge c700ddd5e, #1774) bakes a NEW plugin, apps/infra/openclaw/plugins/paperclip-exec-creds, which hands an agent its Paperclip key through the exec environment instead of leaving the key in a file the agent is told to read. That is new runtime code that has never booted anywhere, so it takes the documented dev-first gate rather than a simultaneous pin. Promote prod only after a dev container boots c700ddd and the plugin activates. ORDERING NOTE: the config half of this change (plugins.entries.paperclip-exec-creds.enabled) is safe to ship AHEAD of the image and already is — the activation planner iterates disk-discovered `registry.plugins` and applies config to those, so an entry naming a plugin absent from the running image is never iterated and cannot fail boot. Config-ahead-of-image is order-safe; image-ahead-of-config just leaves the plugin idle. The PRIOR pin ce1908b (merge ce1908be) carried three changes described below and remains the prod pin. It carries THREE changes vs the prior pin (9b381a8) — this line previously claimed "SKILL-TEXT-ONLY", which was WRONG and cost two debugging cycles (prod incident 2026-08-14: a boot-failure triage ruled the image out on the strength of it, and had to re-open). `git diff 9b381a8..ce1908b -- apps/infra/openclaw/` is the authority and touches FOUR files, including a 21-line Dockerfile change. (1) BOOT PATH: #1707 changed the compile-cache warm pass from `timeout 60 node openclaw.mjs --help` under a 256MB heap cap to `timeout 120 node openclaw.mjs doctor --non-interactive` with no cap, so the baked cache now covers the doctor graph the boot actually walks. This makes boot FASTER, which is not automatically safe: a large-agent-DB tenant reaches its first SQLite write earlier and can lose a lock race the slower build won (7.2 contention class — one 5s busy_timeout, no retry). Exonerated as a deterministic boot-breaker (dev booted it clean at 16:03:33Z 2026-08-14), but it is a boot-timing change, not a no-op. (2) SKILL TEXT: the bundled paperclip skill now documents the `mode` field (add/remove/replace) that upstream Paperclip made REQUIRED on `POST /api/agents/:id/skills/sync` — without it every agent-driven skill assignment 400s, which it did fleet-wide from the v2026.813-isol8.1 Paperclip deploy until this image landed. (3) CAPABILITY BOUNDARY: skills/isol8/SKILL.md flips what agents are told the platform can do. The prior text stated flatly that no generic external-webhook ingress exists and that push events reach an agent only via channels, email, an integration's tools, or a scheduled poll. It now describes Teams -> Automations: a signed per-trigger URL any service can POST to; 1-click trigger seeding for Stripe/Sentry/Linear/Attio (owner pastes the URL in, pastes the signing secret back); PostHog as the mirror case (signs nothing, so Isol8 shows a URL plus an Authorization header value); GitHub/Vercel/Google self-registering (Isol8 creates the webhook itself, no paste step); Gmail poll-vs-push; and the twice-weekly self-renewal tick for Google watches, which expire in <=7 days. The honest-boundary paragraph narrowed from "no generic ingress" to "outside GitHub/Vercel/Google we cannot REGISTER the webhook for you". This is skill TEXT, so it ships no runtime code — but it is NOT cosmetic: it changes what every agent in the fleet believes it can offer an owner, so an image older than this pin has agents actively denying a feature that shipped. Both envs pinned together by explicit owner decision (single-tenant fleet). This build is also the first since the image build moved back to the self-hosted box (#1762): six consecutive hosted-runner builds OOM-killed the 7 GB VM at the `doctor` compile-cache bake ("the hosted runner lost communication with the server", no failed step, no logs), which is why the fleet sat on a 2026-08-12 image for two days.
